title: Checking the assumption: the Augmented Dickey-Fuller test (a newly-authored op), bit-for-bit against statsmodels

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The ACF/PACF/AR folds assumed a stationary signal; the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test checks that assumption -- is there a unit root (a random-walk drift) in the EEG, or is it stationary? The ecosystem had no unit-root test; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, adfTest. On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel its statistic reproduces statsmodels.tsa.stattools.adfuller(autolag=None) BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| ~7e-15); the statistic (-22.36) lies ~19.5 below the 5% Dickey-Fuller critical value (-2.86), decisively rejecting the unit-root null -- the segment is stationary (no drift over 10 s), retroactively justifying the stationarity assumption of the companion folds.

claims.statement: Augmented Dickey-Fuller statistic (lag 1, constant) of the POz signal
the unit-root null is rejected -- the segment is stationary (1 = rejected)
how far the statistic lies below the 5% critical value (decisive rejection)

validation.reference: The newly-authored adfTest op is validated against the field-standard statsmodels.tsa.stattools.adfuller(autolag=None) on the identical signal. Both compute the ADF regression t-statistic on the lagged level; the STATISTIC agrees BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| ~7e-15). The statistic (-22.36) lies ~19.5 below statsmodels' 5% critical value (-2.86), decisively rejecting the unit-root null.
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored adfTest statistic reproduces statsmodels adfuller bit-for-bit; (2) the statistic is ~19.5 below the 5% critical value, decisively rejecting the unit-root null (the segment is stationary). HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED, adding a formal stationarity test the ecosystem lacked (and which the ACF/PACF/AR folds implicitly assumed); (2) the STATISTIC is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- it is an exact OLS regression quantity, so the ~7e-15 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) IMPORTANT honest caveat: only the statistic is bit-exact -- the ADF critical values and p-value require the Dickey-Fuller / MacKinnon response-surface reference tables (an approximation), so this op does NOT compute them, and the decision here compares the statistic against statsmodels' tabulated 5% critical value; (4) the finding: the eyes-closed EEG segment is stationary (no random-walk drift over these 10 s), which retroactively justifies the stationarity assumption of the ACF/PACF/AR/Ljung-Box folds -- a decisive-but-expected verdict whose value is the certified statistic and the ~19.5 margin; (5) the value is a signal property; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: ADF and KPSS are complementary stationarity tests (ADF's null is a unit root; KPSS's null is stationarity); adding a KPSS op and reporting both would give the standard confirmatory pair, and running ADF on longer recordings (where slow drift / electrode movement is common) is where a non-rejection would actually appear. Documented, not escalated.
